subject: Clarify attack-surface coverage across hosting variants for Acme Corp
messages:
From: Jordan Hale <security@acmecorp.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmecorp.com
Date: Fri, 6 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Which hosting variants are covered in your pen test artifacts?

Hi Olga,

We're preparing our SIG questionnaire and the vendor security review for our upcoming integration. Can you confirm which of Redwood's hosting variants are covered by the penetration test report you shared earlier (hosted API, Redwood Dedicated, Private/VPC, and on-prem packages)? Acme needs a clear statement we can pass to our security team and (if possible) the most recent report stub and a short matrix that maps deployment variants to in-scope systems.

Two follow-ups:
- Does the report include network-layer testing for Dedicated instances that run in customer VPCs?
- For Private (on-prem) deployments, do you provide guidance or evidence of recommended boundaries, or is that entirely customer-owned?

We appreciate anything you can share — if parts of the report are redacted for confidentiality, a short explanatory note is fine.

Thanks,
Jordan Hale
Security Analyst | Acme Corp
From: olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Hale <security@acmecorp.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Jul 2028 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Which hosting variants are covered in your pen test artifacts?

Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer up front: our public pen test summary covers Hosted API and the Redwood-managed control plane used for Hosted and Dedicated; Dedicated customer VPC network paths and on-prem Private deployments are outside of the standard engagement scope, but we do provide a scope matrix and a recommended boundary document for Private deployments.

I'll loop in Marissa from Security Evidence to share the summary PDF and a simple hosting-variant matrix. For your specific questions:
- Dedicated in-customer VPC: network-layer testing of customer-managed VPCs is generally out-of-scope because those networks are administered by the customer; we test the Redwood-managed control plane components and any hosted ingress/ejection points.
- Private/on-prem: evidence we provide is guidance + recommended architecture and hardening checklists; we do not run tests inside customer on-prem environments unless there's a custom engagement and a scoped contract.

Expect the summary and an attachment from Marissa in the next business day. If you need an explicit statement for SIG that we can send to your reviewers, tell me the exact language they expect and we will tailor it.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Hale <security@acmecorp.com>, olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 7 Jul 2028 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Which hosting variants are covered in your pen test artifacts?

Hi Jordan — attaching the redacted pen test summary and a hosting_scope_matrix that maps each deployment variant to what Redwood tests and what is customer responsibility.

Attachment stubs: 
- redwood_pen_test_summary_202804.pdf (redacted executive summary; includes scope of Redwood-managed services, findings severity, and remediation status)
- hosting_scope_matrix_ACME.xlsx (matrix: Hosted API | Dedicated (Redwood-managed control plane) | Dedicated in-customer VPC | Private/VPC (customer-managed) | On-prem)

Key notes in the matrix (short):
- Hosted API: fully in-scope for our pen tests.
- Dedicated (Redwood-managed control plane): server-side components and service-facing endpoints tested.
- Dedicated in-customer VPC: control plane tested; customer VPC network devices are out-of-scope.
- Private/VPC & On-prem: guidance-only by default; we can run tests under a separate SOW.

Laura, can you confirm the target remediation windows and whether there are any open high-severity items that should be flagged to Acme?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Security Evidence Lead | Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 7 Jul 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Which hosting variants are covered in your pen test artifacts?

Marissa — quick clarification for the matrix: when we say "control plane" for Dedicated, call out the management endpoints (fleet orchestrator, auth services, telemetry ingestion endpoints) as in-scope. Also add a short line that Dedicated customer VPC workloads (model-serving instances that reside in customer subnets) are only covered for Redwood code and configs, not customer firewall rules or transit gateways.

On open items: we have two medium findings from April (token sanitation edge-case and an RBAC misconfig on an internal admin tool) — both remediated and verified in our April patch; we can include a one-line confirmation and link to ticket REDW-1357.

Rishi
Principal Infra Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Hale <security@acmecorp.com>, procurement@acmecorp.com
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 8 Jul 2028 15:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Which hosting variants are covered in your pen test artifacts?

Jordan — thanks for the patience. Attached are the two files Marissa noted; below is a short, SIG-ready statement you can paste into the questionnaire: 

"Redwood Inference conducts vendor penetration testing that covers the Redwood-managed control plane and service-facing endpoints for our Hosted API and Dedicated offerings. Network infrastructure and resources that are customer-managed (for example, workloads running in the customer VPC, customer-owned firewalls, transit gateways, or on-premise infrastructure) are the responsibility of the customer and are not covered by Redwood's standard penetration testing engagements. For Private or on-prem deployments, Redwood provides architecture guidance and a hardening checklist; Redwood can perform scoped penetration tests on customer environments under a separate statement of work and contract."

If you want this as a signed letter, we can generate a short attestation. Next steps we propose:
- Procurement: accept the attached redacted summary and matrix for the vendor pack;
- Security: if Acme needs Redwood to test a Dedicated-in-VPC path or perform an on-prem engagement, we can produce a SOW and estimate (I can loop in Contracts).

Let me know if you want the attestation or a direct call with Rishi/Marissa to walk through matrix details.

Best,
Olga
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
